2	
3	## Chip facts
4	- 84 SMs; per SM: 128 FP32 lanes (64 FP32 + 64 FP32/INT32), 4 tensor cores,
5	  256 KB register file (65536 x 32-bit), max 255 registers/thread.
6	- L1/shared: 128 KB combined; shared carveout up to 100 KB per block (static
7	  __shared__ limit is 48 KB; >48 KB requires dynamic shared memory +
8	  cudaFuncSetAttribute(cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize, ...)).
9	- 6 MB L2. GDDR6X ~1008 GB/s.
10	- Peak dense BF16/FP16 tensor: ~160 TFLOPS (with FP32 accumulate).
11	  Peak FP32 FFMA: ~40 TFLOPS. => scalar attention tops out low; tensor cores
12	  are mandatory to approach SDPA/FA2 numbers (~50-70 TFLOPS geomean typical).
13	- 1536 max threads/SM on sm_86 (not 2048): occupancy math differs from A100.
14	
15	## Tensor cores on Ampere (bf16)
16	- mma.sync.aligned.m16n8k16.row.col.f32.bf16.bf16.f32 is the workhorse
17	  (see ptx_mma_bf16_notes.md for the exact fragment layout).
18	- Feed with ldmatrix.sync.aligned.m8n8.x4.shared.b16 from shared memory;
19	  swizzle the shared layout so ldmatrix reads are conflict-free.
20	- cp.async available (16-byte variant, .cg bypasses L1); no TMA, no wgmma,
21	  no setmaxnreg — those are Hopper sm_90a features.
22	
23	## Practical notes for attention here
24	- Good FA2-on-Ampere tile sizes for head_dim 128: BLOCK_M 128, BLOCK_N 32/64,
25	  4-8 warps, K/V double-buffered in shared (2 x 64 x 128 x 2 B x 2 = 64 KB
26	  needs dynamic shared).
27	- GDDR6X thermals on a 3090 Ti drift clocks over long benches; the harness
28	  uses median-of-repeats which damps this, but expect a few % run-to-run.
29	- BF16 on sm_86 is full-rate on tensor cores; FP16 accumulate-in-FP16 is 2x
30	  tensor rate but unacceptable numerically for softmax outputs — keep FP32
31	  accumulation.
